quests.instruction: Which entrance has a latch and is built right into a fence around a yard?
quests.question: Gate
quests.hint: This entrance is outdoors, connected to a fence rather than a house wall.
quests.explanation: That's right! A gate has a latch and is built into a fence around a yard.
quests.funFact: Did you know? farms have massive gates that swing open wide enough for tractors to pass.

quests.instruction: Which outdoor space would you visit to pick a ripe, homegrown tomato?
quests.question: Garden
quests.hint: Vegetables and flowers are planted and grown here in rows.
quests.explanation: Correct! A garden is where families plant and grow vegetables like tomatoes.
quests.funFact: Did you know? a garden is a planned space outdoors set aside for growing plants.

quests.instruction: Which object do you grip and twist before you can pull or push a door open?
quests.question: Doorknob
quests.hint: Your hand turns this object before the door will actually move.
quests.explanation: That's right! A doorknob is the handle you grip and twist to open a door.
quests.funFact: Did you know? some doors have flat levers instead of knobs to make them easier to open.

quests.instruction: Which object makes a sound to announce a visitor, but does not actually open the door by itself?
quests.question: Doorbell
quests.hint: Pressing this button only announces a visitor; it does not unlock anything.
quests.explanation: Correct! A doorbell only makes a sound to announce a visitor; it does not open the door.
quests.funFact: Did you know? the very first electric doorbell was invented over 100 years ago.

quests.instruction: Which room would you climb up narrow stairs to reach, right below the roof?
quests.question: Attic
quests.hint: This storage space is the highest room in the whole house.
quests.explanation: Correct! An attic is the highest room in a house, tucked right under the roof.
quests.funFact: It is usually shaped like a triangle because of the slanted roof.

quests.instruction: Which barrier would keep a pet safely inside a yard while it plays outside?
quests.question: Fence
quests.hint: This outdoor barrier runs along the edge of the grass.
quests.explanation: Correct! A fence keeps a pet safely inside a yard while it plays outdoors.
quests.funFact: Did you know? fences mark the exact property line between two neighbors' yards.

quests.instruction: Which barrier would you hang a mirror or a photograph on inside your bedroom?
quests.question: Wall
quests.hint: This flat, upright surface is found inside a room, not outdoors.
quests.explanation: That's right! A wall is the flat, indoor surface where you might hang a mirror.
quests.funFact: Fun fact: interior walls divide a large house into completely separate rooms.

quests.instruction: Which appliance would you use to boil a pot of water for pasta?
quests.question: Stove
quests.hint: This appliance has a flat top with burners, not a closed door.
quests.explanation: Correct! A stove has burners on top, perfect for boiling a pot of water.
quests.funFact: Stoves can use an open blue gas flame or glowing electric coils.

quests.instruction: Grandma likes to sit alone in her favorite cozy chair to read every evening. Which piece of furniture is just right for one reader?
quests.question: Armchair
quests.hint: This comfortable chair has armrests and room for exactly one person.
quests.explanation: That's right! An armchair is a single, comfy seat, perfect for reading alone.
quests.funFact: It is usually placed in a living room facing the television or a fireplace.

quests.instruction: Which room is closest to the roof of the house?
quests.question: Attic
quests.hint: Think about the very top level of a home.
quests.explanation: Yes! An attic is the room closest to the roof, right at the top of the house.
quests.funFact: People often use their dusty attics to store old boxes and holiday decorations.

quests.instruction: Which bathroom fixture is usually the quickest way to rinse off before school in the morning?
quests.question: Shower
quests.hint: You stand under falling water instead of sitting still in it.
quests.explanation: That's right! A shower is a quick way to rinse off by standing under falling water.
quests.funFact: Did you know? a shower sprays warm water over you to wash your entire body quickly.

quests.instruction: Which barrier separates your neighbor's yard from your own?
quests.question: Fence
quests.hint: This barrier stands outside, between two different yards.
quests.explanation: Yes! A fence often separates one yard from a neighbor's yard next door.
quests.funFact: Fun fact: a fence is a wooden or metal barrier built entirely around a yard.

quests.instruction: Which piece of furniture has armrests on both sides but only enough room for one person to sit?
quests.question: Armchair
quests.hint: This is a single, cushioned chair, not a long seat for a group.
quests.explanation: Correct! An armchair seats just one person, while a sofa is made for several.
quests.funFact: A recliner is a special armchair that leans back and pops up a footrest.

quests.instruction: Which room is closest to the ground beneath the house?
quests.question: Basement
quests.hint: Think about the very lowest level of a home.
quests.explanation: Correct! A basement is the room closest to the ground, often below it.
quests.funFact: Basements are incredibly safe places to hide during a powerful tornado.

quests.instruction: Which piece of furniture has a bar inside for hanging clothes, but is not built into the wall?
quests.question: Wardrobe
quests.hint: This tall furniture piece stands on the floor with doors that open outward.
quests.explanation: Correct! A wardrobe stands on the floor with a bar inside, but it is not built into the wall.
quests.funFact: A massive wardrobe famously leads to a magical world in the book Narnia.

quests.instruction: Which entrance would a guest knock on before stepping inside your home?
quests.question: Door
quests.hint: This entrance is part of the house, usually at the very front.
quests.explanation: Yes! A door is the entrance a guest knocks on before stepping inside a home.
quests.funFact: Fun fact: the front door of a house is built very thick and heavy for security.

quests.instruction: Which object is attached directly to the door and physically opens it?
quests.question: Doorknob
quests.hint: This handle is part of the door itself, not the wall beside it.
quests.explanation: Correct! A doorknob is attached to the door itself and physically opens it.
quests.funFact: Fun fact: a doorknob is a round handle you twist to unlatch and open a door.

quests.instruction: Which storage space shares a wall with the rest of the bedroom, instead of standing apart from it?
quests.question: Closet
quests.hint: This space is built directly into the room, not sitting apart as furniture.
quests.explanation: Yes! A closet is built directly into a room's wall, sharing the same space.
quests.funFact: Did you know? hangers are used in a closet to keep shirts from getting wrinkled.

quests.instruction: Which object is usually mounted on the wall beside the door frame, rather than on the door itself?
quests.question: Doorbell
quests.hint: This small button sits on the wall right next to the door.
quests.explanation: Yes! A doorbell is usually mounted on the wall beside the door frame.
quests.funFact: Fun fact: a doorbell makes a loud ringing sound inside the house when a guest pushes it.

quests.instruction: Which fixture would you use if you only had a few minutes to get clean before leaving the house?
quests.question: Shower
quests.hint: Standing under this sprays water quickly over your whole body.
quests.explanation: Correct! A shower is a fast way to rinse clean by standing under falling water.
quests.funFact: Did you know? taking a shower uses much less water than filling a deep bathtub.

quests.instruction: Which piece of furniture would you choose if you wanted your whole family to sit together at once?
quests.question: Sofa
quests.hint: Look for the long, cushioned seat built for sharing with others.
quests.explanation: Yes! A sofa is built long enough for several family members to sit together comfortably.
quests.funFact: Another common word for a sofa is a couch.

quests.instruction: Which appliance's heat source sits right on top in plain sight, instead of hidden behind a door?
quests.question: Stove
quests.hint: Pots and pans go directly on top of this appliance to cook.
quests.explanation: Yes! A stove has open burners on top, unlike an oven's hidden, enclosed space.
quests.funFact: You must be incredibly careful around a stove because the burners get extremely hot.

quests.instruction: Which outdoor space needs regular watering so its flowers and vegetables can grow?
quests.question: Garden
quests.hint: Look for the space planted with rows of flowers or vegetables.
quests.explanation: Yes! A garden needs regular watering to help its flowers and vegetables grow well.
quests.funFact: Did you know? vegetable gardens can provide a family with fresh food all summer.

quests.instruction: Which part of a home often has family photos hanging along its walls?
quests.question: Hallway
quests.hint: This part of a home is a flat walkway, not a set of steps.
quests.explanation: Yes! A hallway often has family photos hanging along its flat walls.
quests.funFact: Did you know? people often hang family photos or mirrors on hallway walls.

quests.instruction: Which entrance keeps a fenced yard closed off until someone pushes it open?
quests.question: Gate
quests.hint: This entrance is part of a fence, not part of the house.
quests.explanation: Correct! A gate keeps a fenced yard closed until it is pushed open.
quests.funFact: Fun fact: a gate is a swinging door built right into a fence.

quests.instruction: Which outdoor space might have a swing set or a spot for a picnic blanket?
quests.question: Yard
quests.hint: This open, grassy area is used for playing rather than planting rows of vegetables.
quests.explanation: Correct! A yard is open grassy space perfect for a swing set or picnic blanket.
quests.funFact: Fun fact: the front yard is usually beautifully landscaped to look nice for the street.

quests.instruction: Which part of a home connects the ground floor to the floor above it?
quests.question: Stairs
quests.hint: You use this part of the home to travel up or down between floors.
quests.explanation: Correct! Stairs connect the ground floor of a home to the floor above it.
quests.funFact: The flat part of the stair you step on is called the 'tread'.

quests.instruction: Which appliance would you use to bake a whole loaf of bread until it turns golden?
quests.question: Oven
quests.hint: This appliance surrounds the bread with hot air on every side.
quests.explanation: Correct! An oven surrounds food with heat so bread bakes evenly all the way through.
quests.funFact: You have to wear thick oven mitts to safely pull hot pans out of the oven.

quests.instruction: Which fixture do you fill up with water before climbing in to sit down and soak?
quests.question: Bathtub
quests.hint: Think of the fixture you fill up rather than stand underneath.
quests.explanation: Yes! You fill a bathtub with water first, then climb in to sit and soak.
quests.funFact: Did you know? adding special soap to a running bathtub creates thousands of fluffy bubbles.

quests.instruction: Which barrier helps hold up the roof of a house from the inside?
quests.question: Wall
quests.hint: This barrier is a part of the house itself, not the yard outside.
quests.explanation: Correct! A wall helps hold up the roof and keeps each room separate inside a house.
quests.funFact: Fun fact: walls are usually built with wooden studs and covered with drywall.
